input.sha256_scope: The dense-small.png file; low-contrast.png is dd4c7ae77cc721466cdc5ad65776d120b95de8674a62babdd743e8ad937fa9d7 and thin-strokes.png is aa39e45edabe856d8318760f77c629e30bbe3a64f625f0e4eeb4b55139f2d4d6. Each page's decoded BGR digest is additionally pinned in expected.json.
input.provenance: Generated by tools/generate_jpeg_delta_corpus.py: three synthetic grayscale text pages rendered with DejaVu Sans, one per regime the IMG-003 measurement doc named as untested (dense small text, low contrast, thin strokes). No upstream code is executed and no external image enters the repository.

upstream.capture_method: Generated input, not a capture: the pages exist so the opt-in jpeg_delta_gate probe can measure perturbation consequences through the whole pipeline on regimes the benchmark page does not cover.

limitations: The committed expectation is decoder-level only: each page's decoded BGR digest. Detection and recognition results on these pages are deliberately not committed, because the delta probe measures self-consistency (baseline versus perturbed through one loaded engine), not absolute accuracy, and the probe requires explicitly provisioned models.
Synthetic renderings, not scans: no skew, no sensor noise, no real-world compression history. The regimes are chosen to stress the detector threshold, not to represent a corpus of real documents.
Regenerating the pages requires DejaVu Sans and reproduces the committed pixels only with a matching font version; the committed PNGs are the fixture, the generator is provenance.
